title: Using AI as a teacher. ChatGPT or Claude?
author: TurbulentForm2163
selftext: Which one do you guys recommend? To learn blender and unity?

comments.author: zenmatrix83
comments.body: both at this point are equally as good for learning, if you do it from the ui I think both show you the links it uses for reference you can read

comments.author: Three_Tails_Studio
comments.body: My opinion is that Claude is vastly superior using the Blender/Unity MCP's.

comments.author: Masterkiefs
comments.body:
If you are looking specifically for a learning AI, I would recommend heyclicky. This is for actually learning/education

Alternatively, just use the MCP and prompt via Claude opus 5.5. Astra works too, for usage and quality I lean to Claude. Astra can still audit tho.

Hope this helps

comments.author: Drunkendrakon6
comments.body: Claude. I build the tools myself and then teach the kids how they can do the same.

comments.author: SalivaSpittingWorm
comments.body: Sorry :D lol Claude, for sure. Better vocabulary.

comments.author: AuralithDev
comments.body: I would honestly recommend claude for this. I use GPT occasionally these days and it's gotten a lot better since I was using it regularly, but claude code can do a lot in a terminal window. If you're just looking to learn, I think claude is maybe best with the MCP's. The only caution I would recommend is that if you're looking to learn, claude really can at this point do most of what you may want in those environments. The temptation to just use them to do it for you can be overwhelming... so be careful.

replies.author: TurbulentForm2163
replies.body: Is Claude really that much better? It’s for self learning not to teach a classroom

replies.author: PacketOfCrispsStudio
replies.body:
I find it not so great for teaching, but more for doing. But im more of a visual learner so would go to youtube or find an udemy class. That's how I originally learned the basics of unity and C#.

Plenty of resources available so good luck!

replies.author: AuralithDev
replies.body: Not sure why there are so many downvotes on this thread. I think theres probably some AI haters that actually just come through here and downvote everything they see... To answer your question... For some things. I'm an AI engineer. Been engineering for over 14 years. If you have a good enough harness and use claude code in terminal, it can literally completely take control of a device and do everything including applications given an MCP... I literally did it yesterday for work to completely reconfigure a touch screen monitor running android 4.4. Like I said... If you want to learn, make sure you actually use it to do that. I'm helping you by telling you though, whatever you want to learn, it almost certainly can already do on its own.

comments.author: zanemoore575
comments.body: I’ve always found Claude better at the technical details, but ChatGPT can be better for image generation obviously and brainstorming ideas. ChatGPT is like a mate to yarn to, Claude is like the technical engineer that gets shit done.

replies.author: TurbulentForm2163
replies.body: So Claude can be more like a professor and chat more like an assistant?

replies.author: zanemoore575
replies.body: Yeah totally! It’s methods of teaching software and how things work is really good if you ask it to explain things clearly, and in plain English. It’s hard to say one is better than the other. They’re both just different and give different responses. Sometimes I find it interesting giving the same question to both and comparing :)

comments.author: impulsivetre
comments.body: I've found ChatGPT to not be verbose when explaining things

comments.author: I_pee_in_shower
comments.body: It doesn’t matter. What matters is the framing. I use both and own a learning tech company.

replies.author: TurbulentForm2163
replies.body: Any advice? I’m using it to teach myself the skills needed to help make a game.

replies.author: I_pee_in_shower
replies.body: Use chat to create prompts to create knowledge bases that persist. Then build reusable skills.

replies.author: Fizassist1
replies.body: you own a learning tech company?  im intrigued (im a teacher)

replies.author: I_pee_in_shower
replies.body:
Yeah, a not successful one :)

The first version try to get a grant from the government for game based learning.

The second one made a chess game (on Steam and iOS) and a math game.

The third incarnation involves game finding books into games; I’ve basically made a Pokémon/Undertale clone 2-D RPG where you can learn math, chess, and languages. That’s currently and development.

I’m also an engineering director and a PhD student focused on Agentic AI.

Happy to help if you want.

Edit: iOS dictation sucks, so had to correct some words that changed the context.
